overview: Bank of Chongqing is a Chinese city commercial bank headquartered in Chongqing, Western China, listed on both the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (H-shares, 01963) since 2013 and the Shanghai Stock Exchange (A-shares, 601963) since 2021. It operates 205-206 outlets across Chongqing municipality and the neighboring provinces of Sichuan, Guizhou and Shaanxi, offering corporate banking, retail banking and treasury/financial markets services, and crossed the RMB1 trillion total-asset threshold during 2025 (RMB1,033.7bn at FY2025, RMB1,108.9bn at H1 2026). It is roughly 1/3-owned by Chongqing Yufu (a municipal state asset operator), making it a quasi-policy instrument for regional economic development as well as a commercial lender.

business_model.summary: Classic city-commercial-bank spread lending model: net interest income (driven by a loan book skewed toward corporate/infrastructure-adjacent lending funded by customer deposits and interbank/bond issuance) is the dominant revenue source (~85% of operating income in FY2025), supplemented by fee and commission income (wealth management agency, settlement, guarantees) and treasury/trading gains. Revenue is recurring in nature (interest accrual) but highly sensitive to PBOC rate policy and loan volume growth rather than being transaction-fee-driven like a Western universal bank.

revenue_streams.name: Net trading/investment gains and other operating income

business_model.customer_type: Mixed B2B/B2C: corporate loans (large/SOE-linked infrastructure, manufacturing, leasing and commercial services) now 77% of the loan book, with retail (mortgages, business loans, consumer loans) at ~18% and discounted bills ~4%. Deposit base is a mix of corporate and individual demand/time deposits.
business_model.geographic_mix: Chongqing municipality ~76-77% of loans; remaining ~23-24% from Sichuan, Guizhou and Shaanxi ('one municipality, three provinces')

main_competitors: China Merchants Bank / joint-stock national banks operating in Chongqing
Big Four state banks (ICBC, CCB, ABC, BOC) regional branches
Other listed city commercial banks (e.g. Bank of Chengdu, Bank of Jiangsu, Bank of Zhengzhou)
competitive_position.market_position: Leading city commercial bank in Chongqing with deposit and loan growth that management says has ranked top in the city's banking industry for two consecutive years, but it remains a sub-scale regional player nationally (ranked in the Top 300, not Top 100, of The Banker's global list) competing against much larger national joint-stock and state banks for corporate and retail customers.

moat_factors.description: ~1/3 state ownership via Chongqing Yufu and deep integration with municipal strategic initiatives (Chengdu-Chongqing Economic Circle, western land-sea corridor) gives preferential access to local government-linked lending and deposit relationships
Long operating history (since 1996) and broad branch network across Chongqing provide a sticky low-cost local deposit base, though time deposits are growing faster than lower-cost demand deposits
Only regional city commercial bank scale; no meaningful network effects or switching costs versus larger national banks; commoditized lending product with price-based competition
Banking licenses are regulated, but national and other regional banks can and do compete freely for Chongqing customers

weaknesses: No pricing power — net interest margin has been compressing for years (2.06% in 2021 down to 1.39% in 2025) in line with the sector
Low fee-income mix (~4% of revenue) versus more diversified larger banks, and fee income itself fell 33% YoY in 2025 on weak wealth-management markets
Geographic concentration risk in a single secondary Chinese city/region exposed to local property and LGFV-adjacent credit cycles

Capital adequacy ratios have been declining even as the balance sheet grows rapidly (CET1 ratio fell from 9.88% to 8.53% YoY in 2025), creating recurring capital-raising needs (convertible bonds, Tier II/perpetual issuance)

growth_drivers: Continued rapid loan book expansion tied to Chongqing/Sichuan-Guizhou-Shaanxi regional infrastructure and 'Chengdu-Chongqing Economic Circle' development (credit support >RMB140bn in H1 2026 alone)
Manufacturing and technology-innovation lending push ('33618' industry cluster, '416' tech layout) — technology enterprise loan balance up 60% in 2025
Green finance scale surpassing RMB100bn in H1 2026, plus the nation's first cross-provincial GEP-linked loan and first western-region tech-innovation financial bond
Capital-light business build-out: wealth management, investment banking, treasury/financial markets income targeted as a 'second growth curve' to diversify away from balance-sheet-heavy lending
Digital/AI transformation ('Chong Yin Xiao AI' platform, Alibaba's Tongyi Qianwen LLM deployment) aimed at efficiency and risk-monitoring gains
Consumer and pension finance expansion (Jie E Dai online loan balance >RMB10bn; pension-industry loan balance +120% in 2025)
Potential long-term re-rating if NIM stabilizes (already showing signs of bottoming: NIM 1.35%->1.39% in 2025, NII +26% YoY in H1 2026) and asset quality continues to improve

business.description: 76%+ of loans concentrated in Chongqing, a single secondary Chinese municipality with a slowing regional economy; limited diversification outside 'one municipality, three provinces'

Real estate loan NPL ratio rose to 7.75% in FY2025 (from 5.63% in FY2024) against a total loan book NPL ratio of only 1.14%, reflecting continued stress in China's property sector even as the exposure itself is a small (<2%) share of the loan book
Retail loan NPL ratio climbed to 3.23% in FY2025 from 2.71%, driven by consumer and business loan stress; management has been pulling back from higher-risk retail segments
Wealth management agency fee income fell ~49% in FY2025 due to weak underlying asset returns in a low-rate environment

financial.description: CET1 ratio fell from 9.88% (FY2024) to 8.53% (FY2025) and Tier I/total CAR also declined, as risk-weighted assets (+20.8%) grew faster than capital; recurring need for capital instruments (convertible bonds, Tier II bonds, perpetual capital bonds) dilutes existing shareholders
NIM nearly halved from 2.06% (2021) to 1.39% (2025) industry-wide amid falling policy rates, though 2025 showed the first YoY improvement in margin in several years
Credit impairment losses rose 21% YoY in FY2025 to RMB3.86bn, consuming a large share of pre-provision profit and offsetting revenue growth
RMB13bn-class A-share convertible bonds (conversion period to March 2028) are steadily converting to equity (~151m new shares added through 2026), diluting EPS and per-share dividends over time

regulatory.description: New Administrative Measures for Capital of Commercial Banks (effective 2024/2025) changed capital-ratio calculation methodology; future rule changes could further pressure reported capital adequacy

Chinese regulators have signaled accelerated 'resolution of risks in small and medium-sized financial institutions' and consolidation of the sector, which could mean forced mergers, government-directed capital injections, or restructuring for weaker regional peers

regulatory.risk: Dividend/profit distribution and FX-conversion rules for H-shareholders
regulatory.description: Dividend currency option mechanics (RMB vs HK$) add minor complexity/FX risk for H-share holders

macro.description: Continued weakness in the national property market elevates real estate-linked credit risk even for banks with modest direct property loan exposure, given broader economic spillover (construction, local government revenue, consumer confidence)

macro.risk: Local government financing vehicle (LGFV) credit risk
macro.description: No explicit LGFV loan breakdown is disclosed, but heavy lending to 'leasing and commercial services' (27% of corporate loans) and 'water conservation, environment and public facility administration' (19%) sectors — common classifications for LGFV-adjacent entities — plus large loans to top-10 borrowers concentrated in these sectors, implies material indirect exposure to local government balance sheet stress
Slower GDP growth, weak consumer confidence and low-rate environment compress loan demand, loan yields and wealth-management fee income across the sector

macro.risk: RMB currency and PBOC monetary policy
macro.description: Interest rate sensitivity analysis shows a 100bp parallel downward rate move would add ~RMB1.4bn to net interest income (upside from rate cuts), but also affects OCI via bond portfolio revaluation; FX exposure itself is minimal (net USD/HKD position is small relative to balance sheet)

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Chinese city commercial banks face a structurally challenging but stabilizing environment: slowing balance-sheet growth, narrowing (though now bottoming) net interest margins, and persistent asset-quality pressure in real estate and retail, partially offset by continued policy support for regional infrastructure/manufacturing lending and consolidation-driven industry rationalization under the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030).
macro_factors.cyclicality: High — earnings closely tied to China's credit cycle, PBOC rate policy, and regional (Chongqing/Sichuan/Guizhou/Shaanxi) economic activity; credit impairment charges are the primary cyclical swing factor
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High — net interest income is the dominant revenue driver (~85% of operating income); a -100bp parallel rate move is estimated to add ~RMB1.4bn to annual net interest income per management's gap analysis, while also affecting AFS/FVOCI bond portfolio valuations

recent_developments.event: A-share convertible bonds (potential RMB13bn outstanding) continued converting to equity; cumulative conversion reached ~RMB1.437bn (~151m new A-shares, ~4.35% of pre-conversion share count) as of end-September 2026

Group crossed RMB1.1 trillion in total assets (RMB1,108.9bn), with total loans RMB582.5bn and deposits RMB627.2bn; NPL ratio improved further to 1.11% (allowance coverage 247.31%); net interest income grew 26% YoY on NIM stabilization
Preliminary H1 2026 net profit attributable to shareholders reported at RMB3.518bn, up 10.28% YoY, continuing the double-digit growth trend

FY2025 results: total assets +20.67% YoY to RMB1,033.7bn (crossing the 'trillion-yuan' threshold), net profit +10.58% to RMB6.1bn, revenue/profit grew >10% YoY for the first time in nearly six years; however CET1 ratio fell to 8.53% from 9.88%

Final FY2025 cash dividend of RMB0.4602/share declared (adjusted to RMB0.2797 for the final tranche after accounting for new shares from convertible bond conversion), implying a full-year payout ratio near 12% of attributable profit on a per-share basis reported by some trackers — payout ratio remains low relative to international banks

Independent commentary flagged that the declining headline NPL ratio partly reflects a 'denominator effect' from fast corporate loan growth, masking continued deterioration in real estate (7.75% NPL) and retail (3.23% NPL) segments, with credit impairment charges eroding over half of net profit in some estimates

Deployed a proprietary 'Chong Yin Xiao AI' large-model platform and the Alibaba Tongyi Qianwen LLM across new application scenarios (compliance, mortgage processing, anti-fraud), positioning itself as an early AI adopter among Chinese city commercial banks
Completed dissolution of the Board of Supervisors and revised Articles of Association as part of a broader governance restructuring mandated for PRC-listed banks

guidance.as_of: FY2025 Annual Report (published March 2026) / H1 2026 Interim Report

items.target: Continued progression toward 'first-class bank' status beyond RMB1 trillion
items.notes: No specific numeric asset target disclosed; qualitative commitment to consolidate the 'RMB1 trillion' milestone achieved in 2025 and pursue further scale with balanced risk control

items.target: Grow treasury, investment banking and wealth management as a 'second growth curve'
items.notes: No specific percentage target; directional guidance to reduce capital intensity of growth given declining CET1 ratio

items.target: Lower overall cost of liabilities via deposit term/structure optimization and use of low-cost policy funds
items.notes: Qualitative guidance only; no explicit basis-point target disclosed

items.target: Strengthen risk penetration, early-warning and NPL disposal to consolidate asset quality
items.notes: No explicit NPL ratio target; emphasis on digital risk tools and NPL resolution via 'collection-litigation-auction' framework

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman and management emphasized 2026 as the first year of the 15th Five-Year Plan and a transition year from 'RMB trillion bank' to 'first-class bank' status, prioritizing balanced growth across scale, efficiency and risk control. Management explicitly flagged persistent industry-wide headwinds — 'slowing scale expansion, narrowing net interest margins and pressure on asset quality' — while expressing confidence in regional policy tailwinds from Chengdu-Chongqing Economic Circle development and the western land-sea corridor. No formal quantitative revenue/EPS/NIM guidance ranges are disclosed, consistent with typical Chinese bank reporting practice.

bull_case: Deeply discounted valuation — trading around 0.3x book value and ~5x trailing earnings with a dividend yield in the 5-6% range, leaving substantial room for re-rating if asset quality and capital trends stabilize
Net interest margin appears to be bottoming (1.35% to 1.39% in FY2025, net interest income +26% YoY in H1 2026), which would be a major earnings inflection if sustained

Strong regional policy tailwinds: deep integration with Chengdu-Chongqing Economic Circle and western China land-sea corridor infrastructure spending provide a privileged, policy-backed loan growth pipeline unavailable to non-local competitors

Headline asset quality continues to improve at the consolidated level (NPL ratio down to 1.11% by H1 2026, coverage ratio >245%), and double-digit profit growth returned in FY2025 for the first time in nearly six years
Early mover among city commercial banks in AI/digital transformation (proprietary LLM platform, Tongyi Qianwen deployment) could support medium-term cost and risk-management efficiency gains
bear_case: Capital adequacy is deteriorating (CET1 ratio fell from 9.88% to 8.53% YoY in FY2025) even as the bank keeps growing risk-weighted assets ~20%+ per year, implying recurring dilutive capital raises (convertible bonds, Tier II/perpetual bonds) that cap per-share value creation

Underlying asset quality in real estate (NPL ratio 7.75%, up from 5.63%) and retail (3.23%, up from 2.71%) is deteriorating even as the consolidated NPL ratio falls — a 'denominator effect' from rapid corporate loan growth that some independent analysts argue masks true credit stress

Heavy and growing concentration in 'leasing and commercial services' and 'water conservation/public facility administration' loan categories (together ~46% of corporate loans) raises unquantified but material indirect exposure to local government financing vehicles and China's broader property/infrastructure credit cycle

Single-region (Chongqing) concentration offers no geographic diversification if the regional economy underperforms, and the bank remains a sub-scale player versus national joint-stock and state banks with far greater funding cost advantages and diversification

Fee income is shrinking (-33% in FY2025) and remains a small share of revenue, leaving the bank almost entirely dependent on spread lending in a structurally low/falling interest rate environment, with limited near-term diversification of earnings sources
